final_message:
I built the Ploverdesk landing page, but I couldn't build or view it here: the sandbox blocks `node`, so `npm run build`, `tsc` and `vite` never ran. Nobody approved the design direction; per your instructions I decided it myself, so it is marked **UNVALIDATED** below.

## What the page is

- **First screen:** the headline "Only the invoice lines that don't match reach your desk.", a short paragraph, "Start the 14-day trial" (/trial), a quieter "Book a demo" (/demo), and "No credit card needed for the trial."
- **The example table** (`src/App.tsx:38–85`), labelled "Example", beside the headline on wide screens. It shows the three-way match itself. Rows are the three mismatches from your brief: quantity, unit price, a delivery that never arrived. Columns are purchase order, delivery note, invoice and outcome. Only the cell that disagrees is coloured; a grey last row reads "Every other line … Payment approval." It uses no numbers, only your brief's own words. On a phone each row becomes a block, with every value under its column name.
- **"What happens to a supplier invoice":** four steps from the email PDF, through the match and the exceptions, to the CSV or API export.
- **Pricing:** 290 EUR per month per company, no user limit, 14-day trial without a credit card, data hosted in Frankfurt, then the same two links.
- **Footer:** "Ploverdesk is six people in Rotterdam, founded in 2025."
- **Invented content:** none. There are no logos, testimonials or usage numbers, and the only figures are the ones in your brief.

## Design direction (UNVALIDATED)

- **Look:** the page is laid out like an auditor's tie-out sheet: white background, near-black text in the system font, and thin grey rules between rows.
- **Colour:** there is one colour, a dark orange-red (`#B23A1C`), used only to mark a mismatch. Buttons are near-black, so colour on the page means the same thing it means in the product.
- **Fonts:** no font is downloaded. An EU-hosted finance product shouldn't make a third-party font request.
- **Motion:** only 140ms colour changes on hover and focus. Nothing moves on scroll, nothing loops, and there's no showcase animation; the table makes the point while standing still.

## Files

- `src/App.tsx` (the page), `src/index.css`, `src/tokens.css` (new), and `index.html` (title and description).
- `MASTER.md`: the design system with colours, contrast ratios, type sizes, spacing and component states.
- `preview/theses.html` and `preview/design-system.html`: throwaway previews, not used by the page.

## Checked by reading the code

- **Contrast**, computed from the colour values: body text 17.6:1, grey text 5.5:1 on white and 5.1:1 on the light grey, the mismatch colour 6.0:1 on white and 5.3:1 on its pale tint. All pass.
- **Reduced motion:** the system setting turns all transitions off (`src/index.css:491`).
- **Keyboard and states:** every link and button has a visible focus outline, and buttons and links have hover, pressed and disabled styles. Hover effects only apply on devices with a mouse. Tap targets are at least 44px.
- **Mismatch cells** also carry hidden "Mismatch:" text for screen readers, so the meaning doesn't rest on colour alone.
- **Tokens:** every colour and spacing value comes from the tokens file.
- **Audit script:** I fixed the one real gap it found (the logo link had no hover or focus style). Its other flag, hover with no transition, is wrong; the transitions sit on the base styles. Its 18 checks for generic AI-design habits came back clean.

## Not verified

- **Build:** run `npm run build`. This is the most important check; nothing has been compiled.
- **Widths:** open the page at 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px and confirm there's no horizontal scroll or clipped text. Pay most attention to the table's phone layout below 640px.
- **Reduced motion:** turn on the OS "reduce motion" setting and confirm hovers still change state, just instantly.
- **Performance:** a Chrome DevTools Performance recording during hovers should show no frame over 16.7ms.
- **First screen:** I estimated from the CSS that the table is fully visible without scrolling at 1280×720 and above, but haven't seen it.

Modules loaded: motion-principles, css-native, mobile-principles, tells, ui-ux-pro-max (the lookup script only; its guide wasn't read), design-audit
Modules not loaded: none
